description: Measuring Broadband New Zealand is the Commerce Commission's programme for independent measurement of broadband performance, meant to give consumers information across providers, plans and technologies. A panel of volunteers across New Zealand has test units or software that measure download and upload speeds, latency, video streaming, service reliability and online gaming performance on ADSL, VDSL, fibre and HFC cable, and on fixed wireless (4G, 5G and wireless internet service providers) and satellite, for which the Commission especially seeks volunteers. Test months are January, April, August and November, with reports published soon after. SamKnows was appointed after a 2022 review, and the Commission's 2026 review page names Cisco as the current testing provider, whose contract ends in December 2026, and consults on the programme's future scope. Coverage: New Zealand. Format and access: PDF reports on the Commission website, free; publication of raw data was not mentioned. Caveats: a volunteer panel, so results depend on who takes part; the provider change may break series; report dates were not read. Simulation uses: measured speeds and latency by technology as service-level baselines, and comparison of satellite and fixed wireless performance for remote-area resilience. Related records: the Ofcom home broadband performance data are a comparable panel, and the Commerce Commission connectivity map gives coverage.
